Definition: Whether consumer protection legislation or regulations specifically address digital payment services, covering disclosure requirements, liability allocation for unauthorized transactions, error resolution procedures, and user rights.
Comments: Côte d’Ivoire has a general consumer protection law (“loi relative à la consommation”) applicable to consumer transactions, and the World Bank DFS regulatory framework note indicates financial consumer protection requirements exist in e‑money and payments rules (e.g., disclosure/complaints) alongside national consumer protection law; this supports a ‘partial’ payment consumer protection framework (general + sector rules, but not evidenced as a single comprehensive payments-specific statute in sources reviewed).

Definition: Whether legal or regulatory requirements obligate payment service providers to notify users, regulators, and/or data protection authorities about payment data breaches, cybersecurity incidents, or unauthorized access within specified timeframes.
Comments: Sources reviewed indicate Côte d’Ivoire’s Law No. 2013‑450 does not stipulate a breach notification protocol (no notification to DPA or data subjects specified), so breach notification is not mandatory under the cited privacy-law summaries.

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing an instant/real-time payment system (IPS/RTP) that enables digital payments with near-instant settlement (typically within seconds), available 24/7/365. This includes both bank-led and mobile money interoperability systems.
Comments: BCEAO announced and then launched the Interoperable Instant Payment System Platform (PI‑SPI) for UEMOA (includes Côte d’Ivoire): announcement Aug 1, 2025; tests from June 5, 2025; launch Sept 30, 2025 with real-time 24/7 transfers across banks/mobile money/microfinance. However, PI‑SPI went live with fewer connected institutions initially (e.g., 45 at launch vs larger ecosystem), and later lists show gradual expansion of participating institutions, implying partial deployment rather than universal nationwide saturation.
